newsitem.title: USA: CANADIAN SPOT NATGAS DIPS IN WEST, RALLIES IN EAST.
newsitem.headline: CANADIAN SPOT NATGAS DIPS IN WEST, RALLIES IN EAST.

text.p: Canadian spot natural gas prices on Monday drifted lower in the West due to a plant restart but scored significant gains in the East on the heels of a NYMEX rally, market sources said.
Spot prices at the AECO storage hub in Alberta eased two cents to C$1.45-1.47 per gigajoule. September AECO was talked mostly steady at C$1.42-1.43 in thin trade.
Temperatures in Calgary were forecast to still reach highs around 70 degrees F early this week, according to Weather Services Corp.

Petro-Canada's Hanlan-Robb gas plant west of Edmonton in Alberta was expected to reach full power by this afternoon. The company was not available this afternoon to confirm the plant's progress. The unit was taken off line last Wednesday for a scheduled turnaround, affecting about 200 million cubic feet per day of gas.
At Sumas, Wash., spot gas prices also lost about two cents to about $1.08-1.09 per million British thermal units (mmBtu).

In the East, Niagara prices latched onto the NYMEX rally by regaining 14 cents to the low-to-mid $2.60s. September natgas futures soared to a new high of $2.605, up 10.2 cents from Friday's settlement.
